claims.text: The recorded planner/monitor mismatch left a 44 mm band legal to the local planner but terminal to the collision monitor.
The corrective configuration changed robot_radius from 0.20 to 0.25 m; try the radius slider here, whose circular MODEL footprint differs from the Stack's padded polygon.
The subsequent twelve-run matrix showed no recurrence or regression, but never exercised the corrective band and was not an A/B test of the fix.
The historical 6.2% claim compared planner implementations, not a controlled A* versus Dijkstra experiment, and remains neither reproduced nor refuted.
The internship simulator's reported 4% difference was not reproduced on fixed inputs.
This comparison holds the graph and cost function fixed while changing the search, using the existing Python references.
After the recorded costmap update, D* Lite used 3209 expansions while fresh A* used 1114, with the same path cost.
The extra work on this change remains unattributed; it does not establish that repair is always cheaper or always dearer than fresh search.
The panes here show a first plan on the shared MODEL graph, while the linked evidence contains the recorded before/after costmap experiment.
Recorded DWB completed zero of five static-room hairpin runs, and the stall's cause remains unresolved.
These panes use the DWA-style and pure-pursuit teaching controllers, not Nav2's code or a reconstruction of the recorded hairpin outcome.
Historical Run 15 had a valid global path while the robot's localization belief was 3.4 m from truth.
Nine later Stack runs reproduced the invalid-local-path mechanism, but did not reproduce the exact historical zero-of-819 symptom.
The shared MODEL relocation here compares localization filters and is not a replay of Run 15.
